clue.text: Mercy shown by men producing old weapon

parts.note: to give quarter is to show mercy to a beaten enemy
the staff are the people employed, the men on the payroll

explanation.surface: Soldiers show clemency and bring out an antique arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A long wooden pole used as a fighting stick by English peasants in past centuries.

clue.text: Tobacco crime making a profit

parts.note: a quid is a plug of chewing tobacco
a sin is a wrongdoing, a moral crime

explanation.surface: Smuggling tobacco turns out to be lucrative.
explanation.walkthrough: QUIDS IN is British slang for being in profit; a quid is also slang for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: British idiom for being ahead financially, having come out with money gained.

clue.text: Related person needing another spell in the BBC

definitions.meaning: a parent's sister, a family relation

definitions.text: needing another spell in the BBC
definitions.meaning: the BBC's nickname is Auntie; with a different spelling it becomes this word

explanation.walkthrough: 'Auntie' is the affectionate British nickname for the BBC; 'spell' here means spelling, not magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for a parent's sister, a relative by family.

clue.text: Dance craze of the Renaissance

parts.note: not a fashionable dance but a mania: a compulsion to dance that swept southern Italy, blamed on spider bites

explanation.walkthrough: 'Craze' suggests a fad; it is literal madness, the dancing mania once thought caused by a tarantula's bite.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical hysteria of uncontrollable dancing in Italy from the fifteenth to seventeenth centuries.

clue.text: Run away in this?

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
out means away, not at home

explanation.surface: A question about the kind of defeat in which soldiers flee.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: in a rout the losers run away.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorderly retreat of a beaten force, or an overwhelming defeat.

clue.text: Top places for driving with success?'That's about right

parts.note: golfers drive off from tees

indicators.note: about means the word for success goes around the letter for right

parts.note: a hit is a success, as of a song or show

explanation.surface: A golfer reflects that hitting off well from the tee is about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside HIT to give HIRT. 'Top' is a garment, not a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual garment worn on the upper body is called a top.

clue.text: Money I have is in francs

indicators.note: is in tells us the contraction sits inside the abbreviation for francs

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for francs
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone abroad says all their cash is in French currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money' is British slang here: a five-pound note; the franc was France's currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-pound note is British slang for a sum of money.

clue.text: Molly and I go out without Joy

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of these words are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two friends head out, leaving their companion Joy behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joy' looks like a name, matching Molly; it is the plain noun. 'out' rearranges MOLLYIGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a cheerless, dejected manner means doing it without happiness.

clue.text: Garment put on as protection for work

definitions.meaning: a coat for the upper body

definitions.text: put on as protection for work
definitions.meaning: a paper cover wrapped round a book, a literary work, to protect it

explanation.walkthrough: 'work' suggests a job; it is a book, whose dust cover shares the garment's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a short coat and a book's protective paper cover.

clue.text: Central Line? This part of vehicle must be filled

definitions.meaning: a playful reading as the inner part of the London Underground

definitions.text: This part of vehicle must be filled
definitions.meaning: the rubber ring inside a tyre, inflated with air

explanation.walkthrough: The Central Line is a London Underground line, nicknamed the Tube; the question mark flags the jokey reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The inflatable rubber ring inside a tyre that is pumped up with air.

clue.text: Dwelling in very seedy area

parts.note: seedy can mean unwell, off-colour

explanation.surface: A house stands in a run-down neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seedy' suggests shabby; here it means feeling ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A large house, often in the country or by the sea, is a residence.

clue.text: Saw a year in prison reduced by exactly 50%

indicators.note: in places the letters for a year inside the shortened prison name
cutting the prison's name exactly in half leaves one of its two identical halves

parts.note: Sing Sing is a famous prison in New York State

explanation.surface: Someone notes a twelve-month sentence was halved on appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is not the tool or the verb but an old proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old maxim or proverb, a familiar piece of wisdom.

clue.text: With fish like trout, hold the mustard

parts.note: the char is a fish of the trout and salmon family
a lock is a wrestling hold

explanation.surface: A cook serves trout-like fish but holds back the mustard.
explanation.definitionFit: A weed of fields, also called wild mustard, with yellow flowers.

clue.text: Notice changes? It's all in the mind

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters of the first word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone noticing changes is told they are imagining it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges NOTICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the intellect, the activity of the mind.

clue.text: A puzzle like this for the Provost of Eton?

definitions.text: A puzzle like this for the Provost of Eton?

parts.words: A puzzle like this for the Provost of Eton?
parts.note: a famous story: a Provost of Eton College claimed he timed his boiled egg by solving this newspaper's crossword

explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a famous English school; its head, the Provost (M.R. James), reportedly finished the crossword in the time it took to boil an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hourglass used to measure the minutes needed to boil an egg.

clue.text: With mouth quiet, one holy man?

definitions.text: With mouth quiet, one holy man?

parts.note: trap is slang for the mouth
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
I is the Roman numeral for one
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A silent monk is a holy man who keeps his mouth shut.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: monks of this order are known for keeping silence.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk of a Cistercian order famed for its vow of silence.

clue.text: Rod and cane used when disorderly? Maybe

parts.note: a perch is an old unit of length, also called a rod or pole

indicators.note: disorderly signals that the letters of the following word are muddled

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster's rod and cane come out when pupils misbehave, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorderly' rearranges CANE into ANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for perhaps, possibly.

clue.text: Organisation of lawmen put in grave situation by political leaders

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: leaders points to the opening letters of the word political

explanation.surface: Political leaders put a police body in a grave position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'situation' is a link here; 'leaders' takes the first three letters of 'political'.
explanation.definitionFit: The international police organisation that links forces across countries.

clue.text: Dispute a regular payment that's split, by gum

indicators.note: split means the payment word is broken open to take the gum

parts.note: rent is paid regularly
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation of 'by gum' accompanies a row over the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by gum' reads as a northern English exclamation of surprise, but GUM is simply the thing placed inside the payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel or disagreement is a row between people.

clue.text: Area producing wine, with litres packed into a special case

indicators.note: packed into puts the abbreviation for litres inside the other letters
special signals that the letters of the word case are rearranged into a special form

explanation.surface: Wine from a region is bottled, litres packed into a special case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' is the anagram signal, turning CASE into SACE; 'a' supplies the opening letter, and the litres go in after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A French region on the Rhine famed for its white wines.

clue.text: Collect, perhaps, rupees hidden by settler

indicators.note: hidden by puts the abbreviation for rupees inside the word for settler

parts.note: a payer is one who settles a bill

explanation.surface: A colonist hides away a stash of Indian money.
explanation.walkthrough: A collect is a short prayer in Christian liturgy; 'settler' means one who settles a debt, not a colonist.
explanation.definitionFit: A collect is a short liturgical prayer, so it is an example.

clue.text: Payment for pages bound to come from King and Queen, say

definitions.meaning: a sum paid to an author for each copy of a book sold
the members of a royal family collectively

explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' suggests obliged, but it refers to a bound book.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an author's earnings on book sales and kings and queens collectively.

clue.text: Foolish people running round cold islands

indicators.note: running round means the foolish people encircle the letter for cold

parts.note: sillies are silly people

explanation.surface: Silly folk run around chilly islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scillies are a group of islands off Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isles of Scilly, an archipelago off south-west England.

clue.text: Decline drinks? Sounds like it

indicators.note: sounds like says the word for drinks, spoken, matches the answer

parts.note: a cat laps, drinks with its tongue

explanation.surface: Someone refuses drinks, and that sounds about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' suggests refusing; it is a falling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or falling away from a standard.

clue.text: Nonsense put on page? Nonsense, indeed!

parts.note: hooey is slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at rubbish printed on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation dismissing something as rubbish.

clue.text: Duck ground up for stews

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read upward, backwards

parts.note: ground means soil, earth

explanation.surface: Duck is minced and put into stews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a past participle; it is soil, reversed by 'up' to LIOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spicy Spanish or Portuguese stews, also any mixed dishes.

clue.text: Pack in point-to point

parts.note: S is the compass point south
W is the compass point west

explanation.surface: Hunting riders pack up at a point-to-point race.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is a British amateur horse race; here 'point' means a compass direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow luggage is to pack it away.

clue.text: American Indians quietly and stealthily move

parts.note: the Cree are a North American people
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: Native Americans move silently and stealthily.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep is to go slowly and quietly to avoid notice.

clue.text: Power obscured, initially? Latent one, possibly

definitions.text: Power obscured, initially? Latent one, possibly

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of the first two words
possibly signals the letters of latent and the numeral are arranged another way

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A riddle about hidden strength that has yet to show itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives PO; 'possibly' rearranges LATENT plus I into TENTIAL. The whole clue describes the meaning too.
explanation.definitionFit: Capacity not yet realised, hidden strength waiting to emerge.

clue.text: Chicken and cow awarded to leader of French race

definitions.text: awarded to leader of French race

parts.note: chicken and yellow both mean cowardly
a Jersey is a breed of dairy cow

explanation.surface: Farm animals are given a prize for leading a French race.
explanation.walkthrough: The French race is the Tour de France, whose leader wears this.
explanation.definitionFit: The garment worn by the overall leader of the Tour de France cycle race.
